source.name: Arrow keys in a tab list must move keyboard focus to the newly selected tab
source.scope: Real upstream bug (https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/pull/37200) at 0a5f6e078c9cb9ecca9ab90b3984c5f792a11bae. Blind to the maintainers' fix d49d8ce583f6f12552f122122a99063738656cd9; routing auto.

journey.title: Walk the settings tabs with arrow keys
journey.goal: Each arrow press selects and focuses the next tab

functionalJourney.title: Switch settings sections with the mouse
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking a tab shows its panel

guards.title: Tab from the active tab into its panel
guards.goal: Tab leaves the tab list for the active panel

plan.root_cause: The ArrowRight keydown handler in Tab prevents default focus movement and activates the next tab via show(), but does not move focus to the newly activated tab, leaving focus on the previously blurred tab or the body element.
plan.repair_strategy: After activating the next tab with show(), explicitly focus the next tab button to satisfy ARIA tablist keyboard navigation expectations.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: ArrowRight and ArrowLeft keystrokes will move focus to the adjacent tab button, updating aria-selected and making the tab operable via keyboard as required by WCAG 2.1.1 and ARIA Authoring Practices.
functional_risks: Duplicate focus calls if show() were to focus the element in the future (currently it does not).
Potential focus on a disabled tab if the disabled check fails (unlikely).
Minimal performance overhead from an extra focus() call.
verification_requirements: After ArrowRight from #tab-account, focus moves to #tab-notifications and its aria-selected becomes true.
After second ArrowRight from #tab-notifications, focus moves to #tab-billing and its aria-selected becomes true.
Regression guard: Tabbing from an active tab into its panel must keep the tab's aria-selected true.
ArrowLeft and ArrowUp/DOWN navigation continue to work as expected.
